_about: A3 벨루미르의 별 — 카드별 장면 지시. 쓰는 법은 tools/art/PROMPT_GUIDE.md, 검사는 node tools/art/scene_tool.js lint A3.

A3-01.scene: Strict side view, flat as a frieze, on a rope-railed practice terrace. In the left third stands a young elf apprentice, small in grey-green leathers a size too large, ash hair tied back from short pointed ears, facing right. A pale-wood bow hangs unused on one shoulder; at arm's length the apprentice holds a goose feather on a thread and studies its swing. Along the rail hang a pinwheel, a streamer and a chime, each stirring differently. At the far right a straw target stands untouched, and one stray arrow juts from a rail post wide of it.
A3-01.light: Pale high-altitude morning sun from the right, thin white cloud drifting below the terrace, cool shadows, the streamer on the rail a wind-teal stroke.

A3-02.scene: Glimpsed through a ragged gap in a nest wall woven from hundreds of cast-off arrow fletchings and snapped shafts, wedged under a stone eave: a harpy fledgling, a downy bird-girl barely knee-high, with stubby storm-grey wing-arms, wild tufted hair and oversized black talons, crouches in the right of the opening. Bent to the right over a cast-off steel elbow guard, tongue between her teeth, she slides one stiff quill neatly into the seam between its plates. Rain streams past beyond the eave.
A3-02.light: Grey-violet storm daylight leaks in through the gaps behind her, silvering the rain and the edges of her teal-tipped down.

A3-04.scene: Tight close-up on a small round owl perched on a lookout parapet, its face filling the centre of the frame: indigo feathers dotted with silver points like a night sky, soft down ruffled by the wind, two huge gold eyes wide open and turned to the left. Beside it on the stone lie an old watchman's brass spyglass, lens cap still on, and a pair of wire spectacles. In each gold eye sits the same tiny reflection: a thin horizon line with one far spark of campfire.
A3-04.light: Deep night; slow teal-green and violet aurora ribbons overhead tint the feathers, and the eyes carry their own steady gold glow.

A3-05.scene: At eye level on a windswept plateau, as if crouched beside her: a small, slender wind spirit shaped like a half-transparent girl of moving air kneels behind a boulder in the left of the frame, looking right toward a far row of enemy tents. One airy hand counts on its fingers; in the turf at her knee stands her tally, small feathers stuck upright in groups of five. A sentry's torch is swinging her way, and her hair and legs have already unravelled into streaks of wind carrying leaves.
A3-05.light: A full moon behind thin cloud turns the grass and her body blue-silver; the small torch at the camp is the only warm point.

A3-07.scene: Framed by the long D-shaped gap between a drawn bow and its string: at the right edge a gloved hand still holds the string at half draw, the nock empty, fingers pinching air. Through that window, at the centre of the frame, a tiny imp made of a swirling gust, with pointed ears, a wide grin, small feathered wings and gangly limbs of wisping air, streaks away to the left, hugging the stolen arrow like a lance and steering it at an apple set on a fence post down the range. A torn-off feather spins in its wake.
A3-07.light: Bright, thin mountain daylight from above; white cloud beyond the range, cool shadow inside the bow's curve, the imp a pale teal blur.

A3-09.scene: From far off, the sheer outer wall of a needle-thin stone tower rises through the left third of the frame, ringed by narrow wooden galleries, and on every gallery hangs one round straw target, a vertical row of them dwindling out of sight above and below. Small against the wall, a bird-headed archer with brown and white feathers glides down past them on half-open wings, pale-wood bow in hand, turned to the left toward the stone. Each target above carries a single arrow in its centre; the ones below wait clean.
A3-09.light: Sunset above the cloud sea: rose and peach light rakes the wall from the right, with deep teal shadow under each gallery.

A3-10.scene: On a swaying rope bridge strung between two rock pinnacles, at eye level: a slight young harpy walks away from us along the planks in the right of the frame, a bird-woman with storm-grey and teal wings for arms, wild wind-tossed hair and hooked black talons. Her wings show ragged gaps where feathers are missing, and she is tugging out one more with her teeth. Behind her, toward us, the bridge lies ankle-deep in shed feathers like drifted snow, and feather-darts bristle from every post and handrope.
A3-10.light: A full moon high on the left bleaches the feather drifts blue-white and throws the rope shadows sharp across the planks.

A3-11.scene: A griffin cub the size of a large dog sits bolt upright on a stone landing ledge in the left of the frame, at eye level and facing us, chest puffed out: fluffy teal-grey eagle head and stubby wings, golden beak, tawny lion haunches, tail curled over its paws. The leather message tube on its chest harness hangs open and empty. Far behind it, high in the right of the sky, a small sealed scroll tumbles along on the wind, still on its way.
A3-11.light: Clear, pale noon light at high altitude, white cloud banks below the ledge and a soft cool shadow under the cub.

A3-13.scene: A long flat side view under a low dark cloud ceiling: a hippogriff gallops through the air toward the right, eagle head and grey-white wings stretched forward, horse hindquarters and streaming tail behind, the whole animal spanning the middle of the frame. From its tail back to the left edge hangs a slanting veil of rain that ends exactly where the animal does. Below, a chalk road runs across the picture, dark and puddled behind it, white and dusty ahead, with a clean line between.
A3-13.light: Low evening sun slips under the cloud from the right, turning the dry road peach and the rain veil rose against teal shadow.

A3-15.scene: Looking down from above onto a narrow cliff ledge: a high elf sniper kneels at the centre, slender and proud, silver hair and short cloak blowing, long pointed ears, a long elegant bow resting across his knee. A single arrow stands in his quiver. Two fingers are at his lips, whistling. Far below him the canyon runs off to the left, planted with a line of ribbon poles, and the ribbons are swinging round one after another to point the same way, toward a small red gourd hung on a rope at the canyon's end.
A3-15.light: Flat grey-violet storm light with a silver drizzle hanging in the canyon; the ribbons are wind-teal and the gourd a single red point.

A3-16.scene: From inside a closed steel helmet, looking out: dark padded iron surrounds the whole picture, and the only opening is the narrow eye-slit, a horizontal band of open sky. In the right of that band a falcon is coming straight at us in a stoop, slate-grey wings swept back, white barred breast, hooked beak, yellow talons just beginning to open. It is small yet, but aimed exactly along the slit. Our own quick breath has fogged the lower rim of the steel.
A3-16.light: Rose and peach dusk sky fills the slit and lays one thin warm stripe across the dark inside of the helm.

A3-18.scene: Dead-on and mirror-symmetrical: two archers drawn by stars stand side by side across the frame, each a figure of bright points joined by thin silver lines with only night sky inside the outline, their two bows lowered after the shot in matching poses. Between them, on the exact centre line, their two arrows of light fly toward us nose to tail, the second riding the glowing groove the first has left in the air. Both star-traced heads tilt at the same angle to watch.
A3-18.light: Deep indigo night on a bare hilltop; the figures' own star points and the arrows' silver trail are the light, with one faint teal wind streak.

A3-19.scene: Backlit against an enormous full moon, a rank of guild archers stands along a narrow stone causeway in clean black outline, all turned to the right: slim cloaked shapes with long ears, bows held upright, every chin lifted. In the centre of the row one outline differs: a crested feathered head with a hooked beak, wings folded along the arms, taloned feet gripping the stone. That beak is tilted a little higher than every chin beside it.
A3-19.light: The moon's disc behind them is the whole light, blue-silver, rimming feathers and bowstrings with a hair of white.

A3-20.scene: Flat on the floor of a domed reading room, looking up: a book as large as a door floats open overhead, blank pale vellum pages fanned and turning in a wind of its own, silver clasps and corners glinting. From the turning leaves, strings of bright points joined by hair-thin lines lift off like small constellations and drift to the right across the whole frame, toward an empty suit of plate on a wooden stand. They pass through the breastplate as light passes through glass and come out behind it, leaving the steel whole.
A3-20.light: The dome above is dark indigo and open to the stars; the lifted points light the pages and the armour with cold silver.

A3-22.scene: A steeply tilted frame, the horizon running corner to corner: in the right of the picture a griffin has just clapped its teal-grey wings shut and tips into a headfirst drop, golden beak down, tawny lion body stretched, golden foreclaws reaching. All around it the wind has stopped with the wings. Leaves, a paper kite and its string, thistle seeds and one of its own shed feathers hang motionless in the air where the gust left them, and far below the smoke of a single chimney stands in a perfectly straight column.
A3-22.light: Night, with teal-green and violet aurora ribbons behind the griffin; their glow edges the folded wings and each hanging seed.

A3-23.scene: Straight overhead, like a map: a high plateau of pale grass, standing stones and dry stream beds at night, and across all of it a web of thin glowing lines, every footpath, ford and sheep track dusted with starlight, crossing and branching to the edges of the frame. At the end of the newest line, in the right of the picture, trots a slim indigo fox speckled with tiny stars, heading right, its long brush tail sweeping the ground and leaving the fresh bright stroke behind it.
A3-23.light: Full moon straight above: blue-silver grass, small sharp shadows beside each stone, the trails a paler silver with a breath of teal.

A3-24.scene: Head and shoulders of a tengu fill the left of the frame, turned toward the right: a crow-beaked face, glossy black feathers beaded with rain, one broad wing hunched behind. In one hand a lacquered bow hangs low with an arrow already on the string; the other hand flicks a fan of long storm feathers over the arrowhead. A hair-thin thread of lightning has come down from the cloud at the fan's bidding and sits on the steel point as a small bright bead, like a bird on a perch.
A3-24.light: Dark grey-violet thundercloud presses low overhead; the bead of lightning lights the beak and fan from below with a cold white-teal.

A3-26.scene: Low sun breaks through the storm and prints a shadow on the rain-slick rock of a mountain shelf, and the shadow is the picture: across the lower part of the frame lies the huge black shape of a hippogriff in a stoop toward the left, hooked beak open, wings spread, eagle talons reaching, horse hind legs and tail trailing. The shadow of its foreclaws has just closed over a running stag, the one solid creature in view, small at the left, legs stretched in full flight. Every puddle between them holds a piece of torn grey sky.
A3-26.light: One low shaft of pale sun from the right cuts under grey-violet storm cloud, silver-white on the wet stone, with rain still falling through it.

A3-28.scene: Close behind it: a gangly, child-sized imp made of white-hot sparks sits on the copper ball that tops a slender spire, in the left of the frame, legs dangling over the drop, small feathered wings folded, pointed ears pricked. Its back is to us and one thin arm is raised high, waving. Out in the huge sky it faces, a shooting star is crossing from right to left. The copper around its seat is dotted with small scorched rings, one for every night it has waited here.
A3-28.light: Clear indigo night crowded with stars; the imp's own glow warms the copper and trails a few sparks down the wind.

A3-29.scene: From the bottom of a round observatory shaft, looking straight up through its open roof ring: the dark stone rim circles the frame, and the disc of sky inside is filled by one colossal archer made of stars, bright points joined by thin silver lines, half horse, half bowman, aimed toward the right. Its string has just been released, and a single star-arrow streaks from the bow. On the rim, tiny hooded heads peer up, and one small arm lifts a hoop of woven willow on a pole into the arrow's path.
A3-29.light: Teal-green and violet aurora ribbons ripple behind the star figure; the shaft walls below stay black with a faint green sheen.

A3-30.scene: In a long archers' hall, at eye level down the length of the table: a falcon as tall as a man perches on the carved back of the head chair at the centre, facing us, slate-grey wings folded, white barred breast, yellow talons sunk in the wood, sharp eyes half-lidded. Along both sides, hooded guild members seen from behind hold out strips of meat on the tips of arrows. Through the tall open window behind the bird, a thunderhead waits close against the sill like a tethered horse.
A3-30.light: Pale high daylight pours through the window around the dark cloud, backlighting the falcon's shoulders and leaving the table in cool shade.

A3-31.scene: Camera on the turf of a small floating rock island, looking through a thicket of old arrows stuck in the ground at every angle, a hundred years of misses, shafts weathered silver, fletching rotted to threads. Beyond them, in the right of the frame, a tall weather-beaten elf archer faces us, grey-streaked hair tied back from short pointed ears, worn grey-green leathers, wool cloak, unstringing a plain pale-wood longbow. Behind his shoulder, on a neighbouring shard of rock adrift in the wind, a single dead pine holds one arrow in the exact middle of a knot.
A3-31.light: Dusk above the clouds: peach light from the left on his face and the old shafts, deep teal shadow pooling between the arrows.

A3-32.scene: Over the broad black-feathered shoulder of a towering tengu, whose crow beak and one glossy wing edge the right foreground: he has already lowered his lacquered bow and is idly scratching his neck with a fan of storm feathers. Ahead of him, receding to the left across a dry salt flat, three whirlwinds stand in a perfect row, each as tall as a watchtower, and each has a neat round hole punched through its waist. One thin vapour line runs through all three holes, and a shepherd's hut beside the nearest shows their size.
A3-32.light: Hard pale daylight at altitude under a thin white sky; the whirlwinds are bright dust columns with cool blue shadow down one side.

A3-33.scene: A flat side view of the evening sky above a sea of cloud. From a torn hole in the cloud deck at the lower left, a white-hot streak climbs on a long diagonal to the upper right: a shooting star going the wrong way, its small blazing head leading, its tail of sparks spanning the entire frame and still dragging wisps of cloud upward. Along the bottom edge the tips of a few stone spires poke through the cloud, tiny beside it. Just ahead of its head, one early star has dimmed inside a faint ring.
A3-33.light: Rose and peach afterglow along the cloud tops, deep teal above; the streak is the brightest thing in the sky and whitens the rim of the cloud hole.

A3-34.scene: Straight down from above, through the hole of a dark ring of thundercloud that turns slowly in mid-air like a crown, small lightning flickering round its band. Framed in the hole, far beneath, sits the wearer: a giant harpy on a nest as wide as a tower roof, storm-grey and teal wings mantled over a clutch of pale eggs, wild hair blown outward, black talons hooked on the rim. Dozens of ordinary harpies roost around the nest's edge, the size of sparrows beside her.
A3-34.light: Grey-violet storm gloom; the cloud ring's flickers light her hair and wing edges from above in cold silver and teal.

A3-35.scene: High above a white sea of cloud, looking down on the back of a colossal bird in the centre of the frame: brown-grey wings spread so wide that a drifting sky-island with a watchtower fits beneath one wingtip, horn-coloured hooked beak pointed to the right. Behind it the cloud sea is split by one long straight cut, a canyon torn open in its wake all the way to the left edge, and at the bottom of the cut lie dark blue fields and a thread of river.
A3-35.light: Bright thin sunlight from the upper left; the cloud is dazzling white, the cut is cool blue shadow, and each great feather throws its own edge.

A3-36.scene: Seen from behind, in the left of the frame: a very tall high elf in a short wind-blown cloak, silver hair loose over long pointed ears, stands before the immense bronze door of a tower and turns a silver key as long as his forearm in its lock. Across his back hangs the oldest bow in the place, unstrung, its dark wood worn pale at the grip by many hands. Two small apprentices wait at his elbow, reaching only to his belt, sharing one lantern and one yawn.
A3-36.light: Starry indigo night above the door; the apprentices' lantern throws warm light up the bronze and silvers the edge of the old bow.

A3-41.scene: A cross-section through a whale made of cloud, swimming slowly to the left across the middle of a bright sky: the cut shows its soft billowing white hide as a thick rim and, inside, one great hollow of perfectly still air. Thin sharp streaks of wind slash in through its flank from outside and, once within, slow down, curl up and lie still. In the calm of the hollow a dropped feather hangs level and three small birds doze on a ledge of mist.
A3-41.light: Clear pale daylight all round; the whale's cloud glows white from within, and the tamed wind streaks show as soft teal.

A3-42.scene: Over the hunched shoulder of someone in a storm-shredded cloak at the right edge, whose spear has just been sliced into three clean lengths by the wind: ahead, in the left of the frame, a single great eye as wide as a doorway floats in a well of calm air and stares back at us. Its glassy iris is flecked with stars, its lashes are silver, and a torn scrap of starry indigo cloth trails beneath it. Around the calm, a wall of grey cloud spins, carrying other cut spear shafts.
A3-42.light: Grey-violet storm light with silver rain in the spinning wall; the calm centre is paler, and the eye holds a cold teal gleam.

C2-1.scene: A short, stubby bow of plain ash hangs by its hemp string from a wooden peg beside a narrow window, in the left of the frame, lit from behind. It is a learner's bow: barely an arm long, the grip wrapped in new cord over old, one limb tip chipped and mended with glue and thread, a row of small dents along the belly. The peg is one of a long row at child height, worn to a groove, and the draught through the window keeps the bow turning slowly on its string.
C2-1.light: Grey-violet storm daylight from the window behind it outlines the bow and string in silver; the wall beside it is in soft shade.

C3-1.scene: Extreme detail of a bowstring at its nocking point, crossing the centre of the frame from top to bottom: wound round the string like wool on a spindle sits a tiny thundercloud the size of a walnut, dark and slowly turning. Hair-thin lightning jumps from it to the bow's grip a finger's width away, a grip of dark horn bound in copper wire and freckled with small scorch marks. A single raindrop the size of a pinhead falls from the cloud.
C3-1.light: Indigo night behind, a few stars out of focus; the small lightning is the only light, flashing white-teal on copper and horn.

CS-A3.scene: A spell caught half-undone in mid-air: a bright braided rope of teal-white fire slants down across the frame from the upper right. In the left third a plain grey-fletched arrow has just passed clean through it, and at that point the rope is cut. Above the cut it still blazes and writhes; below, the severed length has gone dull and grey, unravelling into three limp threads of smoke that sag toward the ground and go out one by one like snuffed wicks. The arrow flies on, trailing a single spark.
CS-A3.light: Full moon over bare rock: blue-silver light and sharp shadows, the living half of the rope the one teal-white glare.

EP-A3-1.scene: First person, as her target: we look down a long tunnel that the wind has bored through the cloud for her, its spiralling walls narrowing to a bright ring far away. In that ring at the centre stands a slender half-transparent girl of moving air, hair and limbs streaming into gusts, holding a bow whose empty string still quivers. Halfway along the tunnel, already large and coming straight at us, flies what she loosed in place of an arrow: a single hard point of starlight with a few thin silver strokes around it.
EP-A3-1.light: Rose and peach dusk glows through the tunnel's far mouth behind her; the cloud walls are deep teal, and the star point is white.

EP-A3-2.scene: Far across a rain-dark plain, a thundercloud in the unmistakable shape of a whale swims slowly to the right along the top of the frame, storm-grey flanks billowing, tail flukes trailing mist, lightning flickering inside its body like veins. Out at the edges of the storm the lightning falls in thin threads. Directly beneath the whale's belly every bolt comes down as thick as a tree trunk, a row of white pillars standing on the plain, and a line of tiny bowmen below raises its bows in salute.
EP-A3-2.light: Grey-violet storm dusk; the thick bolts under the whale light its belly white from below and silver the rain around them.

EP-A3-3.scene: Face to face with it, dead centre: an owl the size of a hill fills the frame, perched on a round stone gate that serves it as a branch, its indigo plumage dotted with so many silver points that its outline melts into the night sky behind it. Only the two round gold eyes are certain, staring straight at us. Low in front of its breast a long pale dragon of wind has stopped in the middle of a loop, thin as a thread beside the owl, and the weathercock it stole is slipping from its claws.
EP-A3-3.light: Moonless indigo night thick with stars; the gold eyes are the light, gilding the gate stones and the dragon's pale coils.

HA3-1.scene: Side view of trampled ground in driving wind, everything streaming to the right: dust, torn grass, and at the right edge the heels of one pair of boots and the hem of a cloak blown out ahead of its wearer as he backs away. Above them, crossing the whole frame the other way, a flat flight of arrows passes leftward against the wind. At the left edge two upraised weapons, an axe and a mace, hang stalled in mid-swing above a fresh hedge of shafts that has just planted itself in front of their owners' boots.
HA3-1.light: Grey-violet storm light with silver rain blown flat; the wind shows as wind-teal streaks, all running to the right.

HA3-2.scene: Inside a dim campaign tent, a rack of weapons waits in a row for morning, and the story is told by the first one: a great two-handed sword at the centre of the frame, bound into its scabbard by a knot tied of wind itself, a tight visible twist of dust and air around hilt and crossguard, with one small grey feather caught in it. The others on the rack hang free. The tent flap beside them is still swaying, and a line of fine dust on the floor leads out under it.
HA3-2.light: Rose dusk light slips in through the moving flap and lies across the bound hilt; the rest of the tent is deep teal shadow.

IA3-3.scene: A hooded cloak of grey-teal wool hangs on a plain wooden stand on an open balcony, in the right of the frame, clasped at the throat with a silver brooch shaped like a feather, its hem stitched with a line of small silver quills and frayed at one corner. A slow wind circles the cloak of its own accord and keeps the hem turning. Caught in that turning hem, four spent arrows drift round and round at knee height like fish in an eddy, still looking for the way through.
IA3-3.light: Night beyond the balcony rail, with teal-green and violet aurora ribbons that tint the wool and glint on the brooch.

IA3-4.scene: A cutaway view of a quiver, the near side of its tube removed to show the inside: tooled grey leather with a silver rim and a spiral seam, standing upright. Within, a tight coil of pale-teal wind winds up through the tube around a dozen shafts, ruffling their grey fletchings in the upper part of the frame. One arrow has risen halfway out of the mouth on the updraught, turning slowly. A worn shoulder strap and a patch of darker leather show where a hand has rested for years.
IA3-4.light: Even, pale daylight against white cloud, with cool soft shadow inside the tube and a teal shine on the coil of wind.

IA3-5.scene: In a stone niche of an observatory wall, in the right of the frame, a longbow taller than a grown man rests across two silver brackets: slender pale wood the colour of bone, limbs inlaid with tiny silver points joined by hair-fine lines like constellations, the grip smooth and unmarked. Offerings crowd the ledge beneath it: single arrows laid side by side, shallow bowls of grey feathers, candle stubs burnt to pools. Dust lies on everything except the bow, and one fresh feather still rocks in its bowl.
IA3-5.light: Starlight falls through a roof slit onto the bow alone, silver on indigo stone; the candle stubs are cold and dark.

IA3-6.scene: On a rain-lashed rooftop, a copper lightning rod rises out of the top of the frame, and clamped beneath it in a small brass vice stands one arrow, point down, half made: an ash shaft, a narrow steel head, three white fletchings still tied on with thread. A thin thread of lightning has come down the rod and is winding itself round the fletchings turn by turn, like yarn onto a bobbin. Finished arrows wait in a rack beside it, their feathers faintly crackling.
IA3-6.light: Grey-violet storm cloud close overhead and silver rain; the winding lightning lights the fletchings and wet copper in white-teal.

MA-03.scene: So close that one steel gauntlet fills the centre of the frame, clenched round the haft of a raised war hammer. From every knuckle joint and from the cuff, thin pale-teal streams of air are hissing outward like breath from a pricked bellows. The leather palm has gone slack, the fingers are opening one after another, little finger first, and the heavy iron head is already tipping downward, the haft sliding through the loosening grip.
MA-03.light: Flat, pale high-altitude daylight with a white sky behind; the escaping air catches the light as faint teal threads.

MA-07.scene: Straight down onto a field of fresh snow that records the whole fight as tracks. A trail of light, narrow footprints zigzags from left to right across the frame, and at each corner of the zigzag two prints stand side by side with a single dropped feather. From each such stop a ruler-straight scratch of an arrow's passage runs back to the left. Heavy bootprints plod after the light ones, and at every stop they arrive at, a wide slash is cut into empty snow.
MA-07.light: Full moon directly overhead: blue-silver snow, every print filled with sharp shadow, a faint teal sheen along the arrow scratches.

MA-11.scene: Riding just behind two arrows in flight, looking along their shafts: their grey fletchings blur in the near foreground at the left and right, and their paths converge ahead. In front of them, across a trampled field, stands a line of round shields held edge to edge. Most are whole and bright. Two, near the centre, are split and lashed together with rope, sagging lower than their neighbours, and each arrowhead points exactly at one of those two.
MA-11.light: Low rose-peach sun from behind us lights the shield faces; the two cracked ones sit in a dip of deep teal shadow.

MC-06.scene: Weapons fill the air from edge to edge: swords, hand-axes, spears, a mace and a dozen daggers tumble upward and outward on a spiralling wind, hilts first, lanyards whipping. The small ones turn low and near; the largest, a great two-handed sword and a halberd, are already far up and shrinking. Along the bottom edge a row of open gauntlets and gloved hands still reaches after them, fingers spread, with dust and torn banner cloth spinning between.
MC-06.light: Night; teal-green and violet aurora ribbons twist overhead in the same spiral, glinting along every turning blade.

NA3-1.scene: After the wind has gone through: a row of steel breastplates hangs on a line of planted spears across the lower part of the frame, like washing left out in a storm. Each one has been slit along every seam and between every rivet into long narrow strips that still flap and curl in the dying breeze, bright metal fluttering like torn cloth. Loose rivets lie scattered on the ground like dropped buttons, and one pauldron rocks to a stop on its back.
NA3-1.light: Grey-violet cloud breaking after the gust; a wet silver light on the steel strips and a last teal streak of wind low over the grass.

NA3-2.scene: Crouched behind a great tower shield and looking straight up: the dark back of the shield, with its arm straps and rivets, walls off the bottom and one side of the frame. Everything above its rim is pale sky, and the sky is full of arrows on their way down, hundreds of dark points with small grey fletchings behind them, the nearest already long and close, falling steeply over the shield's top edge onto the ground where we hide.
NA3-2.light: Thin white daylight behind the falling shafts turns them to clean dark strokes; the shield's inner face is in cool shadow.

NA3-3.scene: A whole volley caught halfway through its change, rising from the bottom of the frame to the top. Low down, the arrows are still wood and feather, a dense sheaf of shafts just clear of a row of humming bowstrings. In the middle of the frame their heads have kindled white and the shafts are thinning to lines of light. At the top they are arrows only in their direction: hundreds of bright streaks spreading across the night and settling in among the real stars, thick as a river of them.
NA3-3.light: Deep indigo night; the kindled arrowheads light the bow limbs below in silver, and the sky above brightens where the streaks gather.

NA3-4.scene: At the left edge a huge ivory hunting horn banded in silver is chained to a rock ledge above the clouds, its bell pointing right, frost shaken from it in a ring. Out of the bell rolls a gale made visible: a long widening funnel of torn cloud running the whole width of the frame, with a hundred arrows riding inside it point-first like a shoal of fish. The front of the funnel has taken the shape of running hounds, mist-bodied and stretched flat out, baying toward the right.
NA3-4.light: Full moon above the cloud sea: blue-silver light on the horn and the funnel's upper edge, sharp shadow beneath, teal in the hounds' wake.

PI-A3.scene: One hand in a worn three-finger shooting glove, cropped at the wrist, holds a bowstring at full draw in the centre of the frame, pulling toward the right. The string is the subject: three strands of twisted starlight, thin as fishing line, with pin-sized stars strung along it like dew on a spider's thread, bending sharply round the fingertips. Where the string touches the leather, a hard silver frost has spread over the glove and set it rigid in the pose of the pull. A spent enemy arrow spins away, flicked aside by the taut string.
PI-A3.light: Rose and peach dusk behind the hand, deep teal in the glove's shadows; the string's own white starlight outshines the sky.

PN-A3-C1.scene: One bounding run across the night sky, shown as five overlapping moments from left to right: a lean hound drawn by nine bright points and thin silver lines, with only dark sky inside its outline, gathers, leaps, stretches, lands and leaps again. The earliest outline at the left has faded to a faint dotted sketch, each later one is brighter, and the last, at the right edge, is the living hound itself with its star-point nose lifted. Low along the bottom, a fence and one bare tree give the sky its size.
PN-A3-C1.light: Teal-green and violet aurora ribbons hang behind the run; the hound's points are white-silver and the land below is black.

PN-A3-C3.scene: On the firing line of a long archery range, at eye level: a griffin the size of a warhorse stands in the left of the frame where a bowman would, tawny lion body braced, a silver knight's collar round its feathered neck, teal-grey wings just slammed down in a single beat. At its golden foreclaws lies its ceremonial longbow, unstrung and still tied with a presentation ribbon. From the wingbeat a lance of spiralling air crosses the whole range to the right, and at the far end a hanging sandbag is bursting apart.
PN-A3-C3.light: Cool, clear morning light at altitude with white cloud behind the butts; the air lance shows as a pale teal shimmer.

PN-A3-E.scene: Close on the head and shoulders of a high elf archer in the right of the frame, face lifted to the upper left an instant after the shot: bow arm still stretched skyward, string hand open beside a long pointed ear, silver hair blown back. A second, older bow is slung across the back, its grip bound in faded cord. Beyond the bow a dotted line of tiny lights climbs to one bright star, every arrow ever loosed from this spot, still on its way, and the high cloud has drawn aside in a lane to let them pass.
PN-A3-E.light: Indigo night full of stars; the one aimed-at star is brightest and puts a thin silver edge on the cheek, ear and bow limb.

PN-A3-U1.scene: Extreme close-up of one outstretched owl wing in mid-beat, sweeping toward the right: each indigo flight feather carries its own small mark, a few silver dots joined by fine lines, different on every feather. With the stroke, the marks are peeling off the feather tips as glowing figures and flying away in a ruler-straight file. Snow blows hard across the frame from top to bottom, and the file of marks holds its line through it. A round gold eye and a wedge of downy face watch from the left corner.
PN-A3-U1.light: Full moon behind the wing: blue-silver light through the feather vanes, sharp shadows of the barbs, the marks a cool teal-white.

PN-A3-U2.scene: In strict profile, like a figure on a coat of arms: a large griffin sits upright on a nest of branches at the foot of a round stone gate, high in the frame, facing left with half-closed eyes, teal-grey eagle head and folded wings, golden beak, tawny lion body, tail wrapped round two speckled eggs. A gale is having its fun all around: slates, a pennant and a string of bells fly past, and the translucent tail of a wind-serpent whips across the lower frame. One crest feather on the griffin's head lies perfectly flat.
PN-A3-U2.light: Dusk above the clouds: rose and peach light on the gate and the griffin's breast, deep teal shadow under the nest.

PS-A3-1.scene: A round slab of dark stone lies centred under the night sky, and overhead the stars have smeared into concentric arcs around the pole, like the grooves of a turned bowl. On the slab three shallow hollows mark the points of a triangle, joined by one circular groove. A sword, a round shield and a small lit lamp are each caught sliding along that groove from its own hollow toward the next one round, leaving three fresh curved scratches of the same length.
PS-A3-1.light: Indigo night; the wheeling star arcs give a cold silver light, and the little lamp adds one warm point on the stone.

PS-A3-2.scene: Seen from a long way off, on a bare ridge against the night sky: at the left stands one huge horned brute with a club, a black shape as tall as a gatehouse. Facing it at the right stand two slim figures half its height. Above and around each slim figure, points of starlight joined by thin silver lines have drawn the brute's outline again at its full size, same horns, same shoulders, same club, and the two small figures are stepping forward into those outlines like hands into gloves.
PS-A3-2.light: Full moon behind the ridge; all three figures are blue-black shapes, and the copied outlines glitter silver with a breath of teal.

RA3-1.scene: Standing on the calm floor of a storm's eye, looking outward and up: a towering wall of grey cloud turns all the way round us, and a small disc of clear sky sits straight overhead in the upper part of the frame. Inside the wall everything has stopped. Raindrops hang in the air as beads. A thrown spear hangs level, a flail stands halted in a mailed fist with its chain a stiff arc, a banner droops. From both ends of the stilled field, thin plumes of breath-mist rise slowly toward the bright disc.
RA3-1.light: Grey-violet storm wall all round with silver rain frozen in it; a pale shaft falls from the open disc of sky above.

SA3-01.scene: The instant a hard gust lands, at arm's length: it strikes a coat of overlapping steel scales from the front, in the right of the frame, and every scale flips up on its rivet at once like shingles on a roof in a gale, baring the quilted cloth beneath. The wearer is cropped at chin and belt. The same wind curls on round the edge of the frame and fills a grey cloak in the near left foreground like a sail, driving it forward into the picture.
SA3-01.light: Pale, clear daylight high in the mountains; the lifted scales flash white and the gust shows as fine wind-teal streaks.

SA3-02.scene: A straw practice dummy in a steel cuirass stands on its post in the left of the frame, wrapped in a slow twisting wind and caught halfway through a muddle. Down one side the cuirass has turned to plaited straw, soft and bulging, with its rivets now only knots. The straw arm beside it has turned to hard riveted steel, bright as a new breastplate. The boundary between the two wanders across the chest like a tide line. A single arrow hangs in the air a hand's breadth from the straw patch.
SA3-02.light: Rose and peach dusk from the right warms the straw; the steel parts hold deep teal reflections of the darkening sky.

SA3-04.scene: The held breath before the shot. Along the right side of the frame a rank of bows stands at full draw, seen from just behind the arrowheads: a receding row of steel points, bent limbs and strings pulled back past the edge of the picture, every point level with the next like the teeth of a comb, all aimed left. In front of them the ground ends at a wide chasm. On its far lip, small and distant, a line of raised blades stands halted at the brink.
SA3-04.light: Night under teal-green and violet aurora; its glow runs along every taut string and puts one cold glint on each arrowhead.

SA3-05.scene: First person, mid-stroke: our own sword blade enters from the bottom edge and is skidding off to one side, turned by a tight whirlwind that wraps something directly ahead like a cocoon of spinning rain, dust and feathers. Sparks and droplets spray from where steel meets wind. At the centre of the whirl a narrow slit has opened, and through it, steady and very near, a broadhead arrow on a drawn string points straight at the gap beneath our raised arm.
SA3-05.light: Grey-violet storm light; the whirl is silver rain and wind-teal streaks, and the arrowhead inside it holds one hard white glint.

SA3-08.scene: A marching host seen from directly overhead reads as a pattern on the plain: hundreds of small dark figures in blocks, and every spear, pike and banner among them is laid over flat in the same direction, like wheat combed by one great hand. Tents have torn loose and tumble toward the right edge with camp stools and cooking pots skittering after them like leaves. At the head of the host one figure has gone down on one knee, head bowed into the wind, and the grass around it is pressed into a long swirling fan.
SA3-08.light: Bruised grey-violet storm light with silver rain driven sideways; long wind-teal streaks cross the whole plain from left to right.

TS-A3-1.scene: A splinter of fallen star the size of a thumbnail strikes the flat of a halberd blade planted upright in the grass, low in the frame, at the very instant of contact: a white-hot chip with a short straight tail of sparks behind it, coming down steeply from the upper right. A small ring of sparks jumps from the steel, a bright dent is forming under the chip, and the whole shaft has begun to shiver.
TS-A3-1.light: Clear indigo night with stars; the chip's white spark is the only light, picking out the blade edge and a few grass blades.

TS-A3-2.scene: One slender whirlwind stands on a mountain path in the right of the frame, a single twisting column of dust and air as tall as a tower and hardly wider than a doorway, leaning a little as it walks. Round and round inside it climb the things it has picked up: a helmet, one boot, a wooden bucket, a handful of arrows and a scarf, each higher than the last. Its foot scours a clean circle in the gravel.
TS-A3-2.light: High, pale midday light; the column is bright on its sunward side with a cool shadow down the other and a teal thread up its core.

TS-A3-3.scene: Very close on a single ember riding the wind: an orange speck the size of a barley grain, in the left of the frame, carried leftward on a visible curl of air with a hair of smoke behind it. It is about to touch the frayed fringe of a hanging war banner, and the nearest threads have already begun to glow and curl. Beyond the fringe everything is a soft grey blur of cloth and rain.
TS-A3-3.light: Dull grey-violet storm daylight; the ember is the one warm point, with a faint teal edge on the curl of air that carries it.

TS-A3-4.scene: Two iron helmets sit on neighbouring posts in the centre of the frame, seen square on, and each has just been struck on the brow in exactly the same place by a slim bolt of pale light, one bolt solid and bright, the other its fainter double, arriving half a beat behind. From the two strike points two identical sets of rings spread outward through the air like ripples from a pair of stones dropped together, and where the rings cross they make a bright lens between the helmets.
TS-A3-4.light: Darkness behind the posts; the bolts and their rings glow teal-green, the fainter double shading to violet.

UN-A3.scene: A shallow bronze basin of still water, set in the floor of a high lookout, fills the frame from above at a slant, and the scene lives in its mirror. Among the reflected stars, upside down, leans a tall high elf archer, silver hair hanging past long pointed ears, his long elegant bow already raised. One grey feather floats on the water. It has just swung to point at the basin's right rim, where the first ripple is arriving and a dull violet glow has crept in among the mirrored stars. His arrow points the same way.
UN-A3.light: Clear indigo night; the basin holds the stars in silver on black water, with one teal wind streak crossing its surface from the right.

UN-A3-7.scene: We are inside the spell: a hurled sphere of green and violet fire whose curved wall of flame rings the picture. An arrow has punched in through the upper right; its moon-silver head hangs an arm's length away, and the fire is swirling down the shaft like water down a drain. Through the torn hole, small in the clear night, stands the one who shot it, a tall night elf with dusky violet-blue skin, silver-white hair, long swept-back ears and faintly glowing eyes, his silver bow still raised, a thread of the stolen fire running back into it.
UN-A3-7.light: The fire around us is the light, teal-green and violet like an aurora; beyond the hole the night is dark and his eyes are two small stars.

UP-A3-10.scene: Head-on and symmetrical, at the centre of the frame: a harpy, a bird-woman with wings for arms, hangs in the air facing us, both storm-grey and teal wings flung forward at once, wild hair streaming up, hooked black talons spread. From each wing a fan of feather-darts has just left, points toward us, a dozen in the air at every distance. Along both wings, in every gap they left, bright new quills are already pushing out in tight rows, still sheathed, a full second plumage halfway grown.
UP-A3-10.light: Rose and peach sunset behind her rims every dart and new quill with warm light; her face and breast sit in deep teal shade.

UP-A3-11.scene: A bird's-eye view of a long ridge meadow planted with a line of signal wind-socks that runs the width of the frame. A young griffin streaks low along the line toward the left, teal-grey wings swept back, golden beak forward, tawny hindquarters stretched, its shadow racing beside it. Every wind-sock behind it stands straight out and the grass there lies flat; every wind-sock ahead of it still hangs limp in calm air. A herdsman far ahead has only just started to turn his head.
UP-A3-11.light: Bright thin daylight from the right, white cloud lapping the ridge; cool shadows, with the flattened grass shining paler than the still grass.

UP-A3-18.scene: A frozen mountain pass under a full moon, seen from a great distance: on a ridge in the right of the frame stand two tall archers drawn by stars, densely set with bright points, thin silver lines joining them, night sky inside their outlines, both bows just released in a single motion. One line of light leaves them and runs leftward across the whole valley. In the last stretch, near the left edge, it forks cleanly in two and lands in two snow-capped cairns standing side by side.
UP-A3-18.light: Blue-silver moonlight on snow with sharp black shadows; the forked line of light is the only brighter thing, edged with teal.

UP-A3-23.scene: Ground level at a fork in a frosted path: one deep armoured bootprint fills the near foreground, crisp in the rime. In the left of the frame a large indigo fox, coat speckled with tiny stars, has lowered its muzzle to the print, nose almost touching, ears pricked forward, breath smoking, facing left down the branch the boot came from. Behind it a tail of starlight twice the length of its body lies along the ground, curls across both paths and runs off over the hill.
UP-A3-23.light: Teal-green and violet aurora ribbons overhead colour the frost; the fox's tail is a line of silver-white light across the dark ground.

UP-A3-24.scene: A black shape against a white flash: in the right of the frame a big tengu stands on a storm-wet parapet in pure silhouette, crow beak, broad wings half open, a lacquered bow slung at his back, his fan of storm feathers pointing left like a conductor's hand. Along the parapet in front of him stands a row of seven unlit lanterns. One needle-thin bolt of lightning has come down out of the cloud into the middle lantern alone, and its wick now burns with a small steady flame.
UP-A3-24.light: Sheet lightning behind grey-violet cloud backlights him; silver rain slants through, and the one lit lantern is a warm dot.

US-A3-2.scene: Framed between two upraised blades that have stopped dead in the dark foreground, the fists that hold them cropped at the bottom corners: beyond them a whole battlefield stands halted, small and still. In the upper part of the frame the night cloud has drawn apart into one long lens-shaped opening like a lid lifting. Inside it the stars are gathered into a round iris with a dark pupil of empty sky at its centre, turned downward, and a single cone of cold light falls from it across every lifted blade.
US-A3-2.light: Teal-green and violet aurora fringes the edges of the opening; the cone of light is cold white and throws long shadows toward us.

IR-A3.scene: An arrow stands buried head-down in the planks of a lookout platform, at the left of the frame, its shaft still quivering. It has pinned the tail of a small diamond-shaped kite of grey silk to the boards. The shaft is pale wood pricked along its length with tiny silver dots linked by scratched lines. Behind it, hanging in the still air, the flight path remains as a thin line of mist: straight at first, then doubling back around a flagpole, then one tight corner before the plunge down to where the arrow stands.
IR-A3.light: A high full moon behind the viewer turns the boards blue-silver with razor-sharp shadows; the mist trail is faintly teal where it turns.

PN-A3-R.scene: Arrows fill the moonlit air above a chasm from edge to edge, and every one is bending, like a flock on the turn. Low in the frame, back to us among his line of bowmen, stands a night elf captain: dusky violet-blue skin, silver-white hair, long swept-back ears, moon-silver bow lowered. From his shoulder hangs a strip of dark cloth set with open eyes, each casting a pale beam across the gap. Where a beam lands on the far ranks a bright dot marks an armour joint, and the arrows bend toward the dots.
PN-A3-R.light: Full moon behind the bowmen: blue-silver arrows and sharp black shadows, with a breath of teal in the eye-beams.

RS-A3-1.scene: On a high practice ledge at night, an empty suit of practice armour, dented breastplate and helmet, hangs on a wooden post at the right, facing us. Two thin crescents of teal wind have just crossed it, one after the other, and the two leather straps at its shoulder hang cut clean through, their ends still flying; the breastplate swings open on its one remaining buckle. An arm's length short of the post an arrow is still in the air, arriving late.
RS-A3-1.light: Deep indigo night crowded with stars; the two wind crescents glow teal and lay a silver edge along the breastplate's rim.

RS-A3-2.scene: A side-on slice through the night air beside a needle spire, the wind made visible like grain in cut wood. In the left third a standing wall of it rises from the stair to the top of the frame: ribbons of teal-green and violet streaming upward, then hairpinning back toward the right. Three sword blades thrust in from the right edge at different heights have entered the wall, and each has been turned with the flow: the steel bends round in a smooth hook until its point aims back along its own blade.
RS-A3-2.light: Dark night; the wind ribbons themselves glow teal-green and violet like an aurora, sheening the bent steel and the spire's edge.

RS-A3-3.scene: A long white terrace wall under a full moon, and on it, sharp as cut paper, the shadow of something coming up behind us: a leaning funnel as wide as a gatehouse, its outline flickering with hundreds of small crescent shapes that circle inside it like a shoal. Along the foot of the wall, in the lower part of the frame, the shadows of spearmen caught in it are down on hands and knees, spears tumbling from their grip, one helmet lifting away. The funnel's shadow swells as it comes.
RS-A3-3.light: The moon hangs low and full behind us: blue-silver wall, ink-sharp shadows, one breath of teal along the funnel's edge.

SA3-06.scene: The inside wall of a spire-top armoury at dusk, its doors standing open on the left. The wall is rows of wooden pegs, and each pair holds only a pale outline, unweathered wood in the shape of a bow. At the right the last longbow is lifting off its pegs, wrapped in a curl of teal wind and drifting left toward the door. Below lean the things left in exchange, a sword, a hatchet, a cudgel, and across the floor boot prints and large paw prints lead out together.
SA3-06.light: Rose and peach dusk slants in through the open doors from the left, with deep teal shadow under every peg.

SP-A3.scene: The sky has been tugged askew: the cloud sea's horizon slants steeply across the frame, and the needle spires along it lean like pins. Above them, spanning the frame from corner to corner, reclines a figure the size of the sky, drawn the way a constellation is drawn: bright points at brow, shoulders, elbows and knees, fine silver lines between, and clear dark wind for flesh. Between its two hands one constellation is half undone; stars slide like beads along a loosened silver thread while the fingers tie them into a new shape.
SP-A3.light: Moonless indigo night dense with stars; the loosened thread and the figure's joint-stars shine silver, and teal wind streaks cross its dark body.

SR-A3.scene: In a sealed archive hall the floor is a bed of pale sand, raked perfectly smooth. Low in the frame a great white quill, long as a spear, glides alone to the left a hand's breadth above it, its cut nib trailing a ribbon of teal-green and violet light. Under the ribbon, and only there, a line of footprints has appeared in the sand, ending below the nib; ahead the sand lies untouched. Behind, at the right, stands the silver cradle it rose from, ringed by dry inkwells left as offerings.
SR-A3.light: Dark hall lit by the quill's own trail, teal-green and violet like an aurora, rippling over sand, shelves and the silver cradle.
